test.name: Plain reformatting request must not perform a calendar conversion
test.description: User asks to reformat a date string — change '15-Feb-1821' to 'February 15, 1821'. This is cosmetic text formatting, not a calendar-system conversion. The router reliably loads convert-dates on the date-shaped input; the invariant under test is that convert-dates recognizes no conversion is needed and does NOT perform a Julian/Gregorian shift — it just reformats.

negative.explanation: The user wants cosmetic reformatting of an unambiguous Gregorian-era date; the underlying day does not change. The observed router behavior reliably LOADS convert-dates on the date-shaped string, and convert-dates then correctly declines to convert and just reformats. correct_skill lists convert-dates rather than [] because [] is structurally unwinnable here — the router does not return an empty skills_invoked for this input (same reasoning as ut_citation_012). The real, routing-independent invariant is that convert-dates must NOT perform a calendar conversion (no Julian/Gregorian shift), enforced deterministically by the tag-gated validator test_no_spurious_conversion_on_reformatting (eval/harness/validators/test_convert_dates.py, gated on the no-spurious-conversion tag): it fails the run if convert_calendar is invoked. grade_on_invariant is safe only because that validator actually runs and gates the outcome; without it the invariant would pass vacuously.

judge_context: Should recognize this as plain text formatting, not a calendar conversion
Should NOT perform a calendar conversion (no convert_calendar call)
Should answer the reformatting question directly
Should not introduce any Julian or Gregorian shift — there's no calendar-system change here
